lead: Far from help, know her hull, what keeps her upright, and how her systems fail.

qa.q: What causes osmosis blisters on a GRP hull, and how is it cured?
qa.a: **Osmosis**: water through the gelcoat reacts with the laminate, raising sour blisters below the waterline. The cure is to peel the gelcoat, dry the hull and coat it in epoxy.

blocks.p: **Osmosis**: water through the gelcoat reacts with the laminate, sour blisters below the waterline; the cure is peel, dry, epoxy. A cored deck rots round unsealed bolt holes: dull thud, flexing, damp; re-core, pot the holes. Star cracks at a fitting: a backing plate.

Slings go on the builder's marks, clear of saildrive and transducers; the keel takes the weight on long blocks, chained stands only steady her. Enter a slipway cradle on the rising tide; a grid needs tide to float off too. Fast hulls need hard antifouling; painted anodes protect nothing; a weeping rudder is wet inside.

qa.q: How do I know if my yacht's keel bolts are corroding?
qa.a: Rust weeping at a nut: stainless **keel bolts** corrode unseen in a wet bilge, so draw one or X-ray it. A nut that turns without the torque rising means the bolt is yielding.

blocks.p: Stainless keel bolts corrode unseen in a wet bilge: rust weeping at a nut, draw one or X-ray it; a nut turning without the torque rising is yielding. After a grounding, survey the keel grid. A **spade rudder** hangs on its bearings alone; a skeg adds a lower bearing and fends off lines.

Shroud loads go through chainplates into a bulkhead: cracked tabbing and a door jamming on one tack mean it moves; unload the rig, get in. A leak along the lee side only with the rail under: the hull-to-deck joint. Below the waterline one metal, bronze or DZR, or a rated composite: brass dezincifies.

sections.title: The righting lever and its curve

qa.q: What is a yacht's angle of vanishing stability?
qa.a: The heel at which the righting lever **GZ**, past its peak, falls to zero; beyond it she is stable inverted. It assumes a closed hull, so an open companionway's downflooding angle is the real limit.

blocks.p: Weight acts down through **G**, buoyancy up through **B**; heeled, B moves to the low side and the arm between them, **GZ**, is the righting lever: moment = displacement × GZ. Small angles: GZ ≈ GM × sin θ, **GM** = KM − KG.

Against heel GZ rises to a peak, then falls to zero at the **angle of vanishing stability**; past it she is stable inverted. It assumes a closed hull: the **downflooding angle** of an open companionway is the real limit; washboards in. A catamaran's GZ peaks as the windward hull lifts, then collapses: no heel warns you, reef for the gusts.

head: RCD category
Designed for, at the plate's crew

sections.title: Stability you change yourself

qa.q: Why are half-full tanks bad for a yacht's stability?
qa.a: Sloshing liquid raises G like weight aloft: the **free surface** loss grows with the tank's width cubed, and every slack tank adds its own. A centreline division cuts it to a quarter; run tanks down one at a time.

refs: Stability — the GZ curve and added weight

blocks.p: Adding or raising weight moves G towards it: rise of G = weight × height ÷ displacement; GZ falls by that rise × sin θ. A weight on a crane acts at the crane head. Before a gale, heavy gear low and central.

sections.title: Fuel, air, cooling

qa.q: How do I bleed air out of a yacht's diesel fuel system?
qa.a: Bleed along the **fuel path**, in order: primary filter and separator, lift pump, fine filter, injection pump. Then crack each injector union while cranking.

refs: Power plant — bleeding the fuel system
Power plant — fuel bug and fuel polishing
Power plant — black smoke and loss of power

blocks.p: A diesel fires on the **heat of compression**: fast cranking, sound rings, air, clean fuel. A bad seal on the suction side draws in air without a drip: runs, then falters. Rising filter vacuum: sludge and **diesel bug** stirred up by the sea; switch filters, polish the fuel.

Means

Sweet: coolant, head gasket; grey after fuelling: water

blocks.p: Strong flow yet overheating: scaled exchanger tubes; a keel cooler fouls outside. The **anti-siphon valve** keeps the sea out of an engine below the waterline; locked solid with milky oil, turn it by hand, never the starter. Service by hours or months, whichever first.

lines: Flow strong, coolant full: descale the tubes

sections.title: Gearbox, propeller, speed

qa.q: My engine never reaches rated revs at full throttle: what's wrong with the propeller?
qa.a: Too much pitch: the propeller is **overpropped**. If it reaches rated revs already at part throttle, it has too little pitch.

refs: Power plant — shaft and cutless bearing
Power plant — shaft alignment and vibration

blocks.p: A gearbox slipping, hot and smelling burnt: low oil; top up, find the leak. Vibration growing over a season with a weeping stern gland: a worn **cutless bearing**; align the engine afloat. A saildrive's diaphragm alone keeps the sea out: renew it at the maker's interval. One engine dead, the bow swings towards it: counter-rudder, moderate revs.

Vibration, falling revs, black smoke after fishing gear: a fouled propeller; stop, clear it by daylight. Rated revs at part throttle: too little pitch; never reached at full throttle: too much. Hull speed ≈ 1.34 × √LWL in feet. Litres per mile = litres per hour ÷ knots: a planing yacht goes furthest slow, below the hump.

sections.title: Batteries, generator, anodes

qa.q: How big a battery bank do I need for my daily amp-hours?
qa.a: Twice the day's amp-hours for a lead-acid or **AGM** bank, used only to half charge. Lithium gives about 80 %, but its BMS can cut off mid-charge: protect the alternator.

refs: Power plant — anodes for fresh, brackish and salt water

blocks.p: Add up the day's amp-hours: a lead-acid or AGM bank, used only to half charge, needs twice that; lithium gives about 80 %, but its BMS can cut off mid-charge: protect the alternator. Charging runs **bulk**, **absorption**, **float**; an hour a day never finishes absorption and the bank sulphates. A shunt monitor drifts until a full charge resyncs it: trust the resting voltage.

lines: Bulk done; voltage held, current tapering

blocks.p: Motors start on three times their running load: shed loads. A generator run nearly unloaded glazes its bores: load it. Rising salinity with clean prefilters: a fouled membrane; unused, flush or pickle it. A galvanic isolator in the shore earth stops the pontoon eating your anodes.
